title: Alan Turing
passage: Alan Turing was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher, and theoretical biologist. He was born on June 23, 1912 in London, England. During the Second World War, Turing worked for the Government Code and Cypher School at Bletchley Park, Britain's codebreaking centre that produced Ultra intelligence. He played a pivotal role in cracking intercepted coded messages, notably the German Enigma machine. In 1950, he proposed the Turing Test to address the question of whether machines can think.

title: Transformer Architecture
passage: The Transformer is a deep learning architecture introduced in the 2017 seminal paper 'Attention Is All You Need' by Ashish Vaswani and colleagues at Google Brain and Google Research. Unlike earlier recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and LSTMs, Transformers rely entirely on self-attention mechanisms to compute representations of input sequences without using sequence-aligned recurrence or convolution. This design enables extensive parallelization during training and forms the foundation for modern large language models including BERT, GPT, and T5.

title: BERT and DistilBERT
passage: BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, was introduced by Jacob Devlin and Google researchers in October 2018. It uses masked language modeling and next sentence prediction to learn deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text. In 2019, Victor Sanh and researchers at Hugging Face created DistilBERT, a smaller, faster, and lighter version of BERT trained via knowledge distillation. DistilBERT retains 97 percent of BERT's language understanding capabilities while being 40 percent smaller and 60 percent faster.

title: Python Programming Language
passage: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language conceived in the late 1980s by Guido van Rossum at Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) in the Netherlands. It was officially released in February 1991. Python emphasizes code readability with its distinctive use of significant indentation. Python supports multiple programming paradigms, including structured, object-oriented, and functional programming. Its standard library is often cited as one of its greatest strengths.

title: Natural Language Processing
passage: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is an interdisciplinary subfield of computer science, artificial intelligence, and linguistics concerned with the interactions between computers and human language. Core NLP tasks include tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, information retrieval, sentiment analysis, and machine translation. Modern NLP has shifted from rule-based and statistical systems toward deep transformer-based architectures that learn contextual representations.

title: Solar System and Mars
passage: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, larger only than Mercury. Mars carries the name of the Roman god of war and is often referred to as the Red Planet due to iron oxide prevalent on its surface. Mars has two small, irregularly shaped moons named Phobos and Deimos, discovered by Asaph Hall in 1877. The planet has a thin atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide, with traces of nitrogen and argon.

title: James Webb Space Telescope
passage: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is an optical space telescope launched on December 25, 2021 aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana. JWST is designed to conduct infrared astronomy and is the largest optical telescope in space. It operates at the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. The telescope was developed through an international collaboration between NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA), and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).

title: Photosynthesis
passage: Photosynthesis is a biological process used by plants, algae, and certain bacteria to convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. The process takes place inside cellular organelles called chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll. The primary reactants are water and carbon dioxide, while oxygen and glucose are the primary products. The overall chemical equation is 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + light -> C6H12O6 + 6 O2.

title: Mount Everest
passage: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. The China-Nepal border runs across its summit point. Its current official elevation is 8,848.86 metres (29,031.7 feet), established jointly by Nepalese and Chinese authorities in December 2020. The first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest was achieved by Sir Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay of Nepal on May 29, 1953.

title: Amazon Rainforest
passage: The Amazon rainforest, also known as Amazonia, is a moist broadleaf tropical rainforest in the Amazon biome that covers most of the Amazon basin of South America. It spans across nine nations, with 60 percent located within Brazil, followed by Peru with 13 percent, and Colombia with 10 percent. The Amazon represents over half of the planet's remaining rainforests and comprises the largest and most biodiverse tract of tropical rainforest in the world.

title: Industrial Revolution
passage: The Industrial Revolution was a period of global transition of human economy towards more widespread and efficient manufacturing processes that began in Great Britain around 1760. It was marked by the transition from hand production methods to machines, new chemical manufacturing and iron production processes, the increasing use of steam power and water power, and the development of machine tools. It led to unprecedented growth in urban population and living standards.

title: World Wide Web
passage: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee while working at CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research in Switzerland. Berners-Lee developed the first web browser, called WorldWideWeb, and wrote the specifications for three foundational web technologies: HTML (Hypertext Markup Language), HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), and URIs (Uniform Resource Identifiers). The web became publicly available in August 1991.
